tasks.short: Record customer inquiries, complaints, transactions and actions in the customer case.

steps.what: Locate the customer case and link the interaction to it.
Copy transaction references, actions and promised dates into the case fields.
Write a concise account of the inquiry, complaint and response.

loop.input: Brief interaction notes, complaint details and verified structured action fields.
loop.output: A draft interaction record distinguishing customer statements from confirmed actions.
loop.check: Match identifiers, dates and amounts to source fields; flag unsupported statements for representative review.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair; on failure retain source notes for manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle transaction facts, but varied free-text complaint notes need concise wording and attribution.

steps.what: Check accuracy and necessary detail, then save the interaction record.

tasks.design: Configure the {HELPDESK} to link interactions and retain structured case fields, then feed transaction events from the {CRM} and {ERP}. A bounded drafting loop turns brief notes into a sourced draft; the representative checks it before saving, with corrections retained in the case history.
tasks.previous_blocker: Representatives had to reconcile separate screens and write narrative notes themselves. Automatic capture could store events but could not reliably summarise varied customer accounts.
tasks.enabler_now: Event integrations can populate factual fields, and bounded drafting can shorten narrative entry. Existing case forms provide validation and a review point.
tasks.still_hard: A draft cannot recover details the representative never captured. Incorrect attribution, unnecessary sensitive detail and records linked to the wrong customer remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the difference between what the customer alleged, what the representative promised and what actually happened.

ambition.what: Handover brief for customers returning to an unresolved case

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time copying transaction facts and writing notes. They can prepare a usable handover during the interaction, but gain no new decision rights.

reach.task: Prepare an accurate case chronology for customer correspondence.
reach.learn: Learn source attribution, retention rules and the distinction between allegations and verified events.

reach.task: Record reported symptoms and actions without losing diagnostic detail.
reach.learn: Learn which facts technical colleagues need and how to distinguish a symptom from a diagnosis.

evidence.claim: A knowledge-based answer system can create a pre-filled request when it cannot answer.
Structured event capture plus a reviewed narrative draft is a plausible design; its savings are estimates.
In the Netherlands, agent recording and monitoring arrangements can require works council consent.

assumptions: The typical record is entered in the {HELPDESK}; no spreadsheet bridge is assumed.
Structured fields support the automation prior, while free-text notes justify one bounded loop.
Brief representative notes are available; full call recording is not required.
GDPR data minimisation, access and retention requirements apply.
National employee consultation requirements vary. The cited Netherlands rule is not assumed to apply across Europe.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and consultation effort where required; approval waiting can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Where are interaction records currently stored?
Which fields and transaction events are available?
Which note categories require special handling or restricted access?
What retention and correction policies apply?
Would the change introduce recording or employee monitoring?
research_questions: Which fields can the existing {HELPDESK} populate automatically?
Does source-linked drafting preserve customer attribution on representative sample cases?
Can each interaction be linked uniquely without merging unrelated customers?
new_work: Review narrative drafts and correct unsupported statements.
Resolve missing events and incorrect case links.
Maintain field mappings, draft instructions and retention settings.
Sample saved records for omissions and unnecessary personal detail.
tasks.statement: Keep records of customer interactions or transactions, recording details of inquiries, complaints, or comments, as well as actions taken.

tasks.short: Resolve service and billing complaints through exchanges, refunds or bill adjustments.

steps.what: Listen to the complaint and clarify the outcome the customer wants.
Retrieve the purchase, invoice, service history and previous remedies.
Check policy eligibility, refund amounts and available exchange options.
Choose a fair remedy within delegated authority and agree it with the customer.
Obtain supervisor approval for remedies outside delegated limits.
Execute the approved exchange, refund or bill adjustment.
Send the customer a written explanation of the remedy and next steps.

loop.input: Approved remedy, confirmed transaction status, customer concern and approved response wording.
loop.output: A short remedy explanation with the correct amount, timing and next steps.
loop.check: Match amounts and status to transaction fields; the representative checks tone and commitments before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; use an approved template if checks fail or the case needs specialist wording.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle standard confirmations; varied grievances need a short case-specific explanation.

steps.what: Record the remedy, update the case status and schedule any follow-up.

tasks.design: Combine evidence from the {CRM}, {HELPDESK} and {ERP}, and calculate policy-based remedy options with fixed rules. The representative chooses the remedy, the {WORKFLOW} requests approval only above delegated limits, and a checked integration executes the approved transaction through the {ERP}, {BANK} or {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded loop drafts the customer explanation for approval, then the {HELPDESK} records the result and schedules follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, approval limits and transaction tools were separated. Representatives had to calculate remedies and repeat details across systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic rules and integrations can prepare and execute approved remedies. Bounded drafting reduces writing without transferring remedy judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Contested evidence, statutory rights, discretionary fairness and failed refund or exchange transactions remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Restore trust, distinguish an inadequate standard remedy from a reasonable one, and explain the decision.

ambition.what: Post-remedy recovery calls for customers whose first complaint remained unresolved.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult conversations and checking whether remedies worked. Any wider concession authority needs an explicit delegation; it does not follow from automation.

reach.task: Review remedy consistency and approve exceptional concessions.
reach.learn: Consumer rights, delegated limits and evidence for comparing similar complaints.

reach.task: Write formal responses to unresolved complaints.
reach.learn: Clear explanations, accurate commitments and escalation wording.

evidence.claim: Support assistants have documented productivity gains, but those gains do not establish safe autonomous refund handling.
Fixed approval limits, amount checks and transaction controls can automate remedy administration.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant where automated decisions have legal or similarly significant effects.
In the Netherlands, specified employee-monitoring arrangements require works council consent.

assumptions: Shares estimate combined handling effort, including supervisor effort averaged across cases.
Supervisor approval applies only outside delegated limits; routine remedies bypass that step.
Only the relevant transaction system is used for each remedy.
The people and judgement priors fit resolution; preparation and transaction paperwork remain open to automation.
Build ranges cover one refund route and one exchange route with supported interfaces.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation follows national rules; employee emotion inference is not part of this design.
unknowns: Current refund and concession limits.
Applicable consumer rights and service terms.
Transaction reversal and duplicate-prevention capabilities.
Availability and quality of linked complaint evidence.
Applicable national consultation requirements and current monitoring arrangements.
research_questions: Which routine remedy checks already exist in the transaction systems?
How are partial refunds, previous credits and failed transactions reconciled?
Which complaints require legal or specialist review rather than standard policy handling?
How much extra review do case-specific drafts require compared with approved templates?
new_work: Maintain remedy rules and approval limits.
Review transaction details before execution.
Handle failed refunds, exchanges and duplicate warnings.
Check drafted explanations and commitments.
Review unresolved complaints after the remedy.
tasks.statement: Resolve customers' service or billing complaints by performing activities such as exchanging merchandise, refunding money, or adjusting bills.

tasks.short: Verify that promised changes happened and adequately resolved the customer's problem.

steps.what: Find cases awaiting resolution checks and read the promised remedy.
Compare promised changes with account, order and case records.
Judge whether completed changes address the original problem.
Ask the responsible team to complete missing changes or explain discrepancies.
Ask the customer whether the remedy worked when records cannot establish resolution.
Close, reopen or escalate the case based on the evidence and customer feedback.

tasks.design: Configure resolution checkpoints in the {HELPDESK} and compare explicit remedy fields with events from the {CRM} and {ERP}. Show evidence and discrepancies together, and route missing changes through the {WORKFLOW}. The representative judges adequacy, contacts the customer when needed and approves case closure or escalation.
tasks.previous_blocker: A completed case status did not prove that the promised account or order change happened. Remedies were often described only in notes, making reliable comparisons difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured remedy fields and event integrations allow exact checks. AI-assisted coding can make those comparisons cheaper to build, without automating the judgement of adequacy.
tasks.still_hard: Some remedies lack observable completion evidence. A technically completed change can still leave the customer harmed or dissatisfied.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish administrative completion from a remedy that actually addresses the customer's problem.

ambition.what: Daily intervention on remedies that repeatedly fail after completion

tasks.altitude: The representative checks fewer screens and sends fewer internal chasers. They can identify repeat failures each day and recommend corrective action; wider remediation authority requires explicit delegation.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Choose corrective action for recurring failures across case owners.
reach.learn: Learn root-cause analysis, process ownership and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Verify that a reported fix resolves the user's original symptom.
reach.learn: Learn outcome-based checks and when user confirmation is stronger than a completed ticket.

evidence.claim: Support integrations can retrieve order facts and execute changes; that does not establish remedy adequacy.
Explicit remedy checks and internal reminders can be deterministic, while adequacy remains human judgement.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions.

assumptions: Promised remedies can be captured as structured fields for common case types.
Internal reminders can use fixed templates; no model loop is necessary.
The judgement-heavy prior applies to adequacy, while evidence gathering and chasing can change substantially.
Correction requests and customer confirmation are conditional paths; shares average across checked cases.
GDPR applies. The design does not infer resolution from a score or make significant customer decisions automatically.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot. National employee consultation applies where required, especially if case data becomes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which remedies have reliable completion events?
Who may close, reopen and escalate cases?
Which cases require customer confirmation?
Are promised remedies structured or only written in notes?
What constitutes a repeat failure and who can authorise wider correction?
research_questions: Which remedy types can be verified using exact fields and events?
How often does completed status disagree with customer feedback?
Can reminders reach the responsible queue without producing duplicate chasers?
new_work: Review discrepancies and judge remedy adequacy.
Handle absent or delayed completion events.
Maintain remedy checks, reminder timing and escalation routes.
Review repeat-failure patterns with process owners.
tasks.statement: Check to ensure that appropriate changes were made to resolve customers' problems.

tasks.short: Tell customers the answer, investigation outcome or approved adjustment and explain sensitive results.

steps.what: Read the case outcome, supporting evidence and authorised adjustment.
Choose the contact channel and whether the result needs a personal explanation.
Prepare the written reply or call explanation from the case facts.

loop.input: Approved outcome, verified amounts and dates, case evidence and approved response templates.
loop.output: A draft explanation containing no new remedy, promise or decision.
loop.check: Validate amounts and dates against source fields; require support for factual claims and human review before external use.
loop.stop: Use a fixed template when sufficient; otherwise one draft and one repair maximum, then manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover routine updates, but varied investigation findings need a readable case-specific explanation.

steps.what: Send routine written updates using the approved outcome and standard wording.
Check the prepared explanation and discuss sensitive or disputed results with the customer.
Record delivery, customer response and any further follow-up.

tasks.design: Join approved outcome facts in the {HELPDESK} and configure standard notifications through the {EMAIL}. Use a bounded drafting loop for case-specific explanations, which the representative reviews before speaking or sending them. Capture delivery automatically and let the representative confirm customer responses and follow-up tasks in the {HELPDESK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Outcomes, financial adjustments and contact preferences were spread across records. Standard notices were feasible, but nuanced explanations required manual preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured notifications can send approved facts, while bounded drafting can prepare explanations from the same case record. Integration code can connect facts and delivery events with less development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Bad news, disputed findings and ambiguous promises remain difficult to explain. Delivery does not prove understanding, and contact preferences can be incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Explain an unwelcome result clearly, recognise misunderstanding and agree the next step without inventing commitments.

ambition.what: Plain-language explanation callback for customers who cannot use written notices

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer routine sends and less reply preparation, leaving more time for explanation calls. The representative can offer the callback service if authorised, while adjustment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare evidence-based investigation outcome letters.
reach.learn: Learn approved wording, factual attribution and which statements create a commitment.

reach.task: Arrange callbacks with the right case owner.
reach.learn: Learn contact preferences, identity boundaries and callback routing.

evidence.claim: Support systems can answer customers through email and voice with connected account information.
The proposed split between fixed notices, reviewed drafts and human explanations is a design estimate.
The EU AI Act includes disclosure obligations for customer-facing AI interaction.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to its specified exceptions.

assumptions: Routine written updates and personal explanations are alternative paths; shares average across the contact mix.
Only fixed wording populated from approved facts is sent automatically. Model-generated explanations require representative approval.
The communication-heavy prior remains useful; preparation, delivery tracking and routine notices can change separately.
Free-text customer responses remain representative-entered; delivery fields can populate automatically.
GDPR applies to case data and outbound contact. Internal drafting does not introduce a customer-facing chatbot.
If an interactive customer-facing AI channel is later added, assess EU AI Act disclosure obligations.
No emotion recognition is used. National consultation requirements apply where employee recording or monitoring changes.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and required access or consultation effort.
unknowns: Which outcomes and adjustments are already approved before customer contact?
Which notices have approved templates?
Which customers need telephone explanations or accessible formats?
Which channels have reliable contact preferences and delivery events?
Who may approve nonstandard wording or additional remedies?
research_questions: Which routine notices can be configured in the existing {HELPDESK}?
Do draft explanations preserve evidence and avoid new promises?
Can delivery failures create a follow-up task without repeated customer messages?
new_work: Review case-specific explanations before external use.
Handle failed delivery, disputed outcomes and callback requests.
Maintain approved templates, contact rules and drafting instructions.
Sample drafts for unsupported claims and accidental commitments.
tasks.statement: Contact customers to respond to inquiries or to notify them of claim investigation results or any planned adjustments.

tasks.short: Refer unresolved customer grievances to the department responsible for investigating them.

steps.what: Read the grievance, previous contacts and attempted remedies.
Decide whether escalation is needed and which department should own it.
Write the handoff summary with evidence, attempted remedies and the unresolved question.

loop.input: Case messages, recorded remedies, evidence references and the human escalation decision.
loop.output: A structured handoff brief with source references and explicit missing facts.
loop.check: Check required fields and source references automatically; the representative checks factual accuracy.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; unsupported claims or failed checks return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can insert fields but cannot reliably condense an unstructured grievance history.

steps.what: Assign the case and send the brief to the designated department.
Explain the handoff, next contact and expected response to the customer.
Check acknowledgement and chase missing ownership or overdue investigation.

tasks.design: Join case evidence from the {HELPDESK} and {CRM}, then use a bounded drafting loop to prepare a source-linked handoff brief. The representative decides escalation and ownership; configured {HELPDESK} queues assign the case, track acknowledgement and notify overdue owners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ownership rules were scattered, histories were lengthy, and email handoffs lacked reliable acknowledgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Queue configuration handles dispatch and reminders. Bounded summarisation can reduce preparation when it is checked against the case record.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-department responsibility, incomplete evidence and promises to upset customers remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the real unresolved issue and secure ownership when departments disagree.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on repeat grievances that need a cross-department process fix.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling histories and chasing replies toward resolving ownership disputes and spotting repeat failures. Process fixes remain decisions for the responsible department.

reach.task: Review recurring escalations and stalled cases.
reach.learn: Queue design, service targets and evidence needed to propose a process change.

reach.task: Investigate a service grievance involving a technical failure.
reach.learn: A reproducible problem description, relevant logs and the distinction between symptoms and causes.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based support software can open a pre-filled request when it cannot answer.
A study of 5,179 support agents found higher resolution productivity with an assistant; it does not establish savings for this workflow.
Queue assignment, acknowledgement tracking and overdue reminders are standard deterministic workflow patterns.

assumptions: The judgement prior fits escalation decisions; dispatch and reminders need no autonomous agent.
Email bridges departments today even where the case itself is held in the {HELPDESK}.
Summary review is included in remaining representative time; approval of the escalation action stays at the ownership decision.
Build ranges cover a small set of investigating departments and text case records.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation under national rules may be needed if employee monitoring changes.
unknowns: Actual ownership rules and disputed boundaries.
Whether investigating departments use the same ticket records.
Acknowledgement and response targets.
Access restrictions on grievance evidence.
Whether national consultation requirements apply to the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which handoffs can existing queue settings manage?
What evidence do receiving departments need to accept ownership?
How often do summaries omit a fact that changes the investigation?
new_work: Review and correct handoff briefs.
Maintain department routing and response targets.
Resolve unaccepted or disputed ownership.
Sample summaries for unsupported claims and omissions.
tasks.statement: Refer unresolved customer grievances to designated departments for further investigation.

tasks.short: Calculate service charges, collect payments or deposits, and arrange billing.

steps.what: Clarify the requested service with the customer.
Look up the customer account, contract and billing details.
Calculate charges and deposits using tariffs, contract terms and tax rules.
Resolve unusual terms, disputed charges or discretionary concessions.
Explain the amount and obtain the customer's agreement.
Issue the invoice or payment request.
Guide payment or deposit authorisation and check its status.
Record the billing arrangement and payment status on the customer account.

tasks.design: Configure tariff calculations, invoices and payment requests in the {ERP}, with a joined account view from the {CRM}. A deterministic integration records authorised payment status from the {BANK}; customers authorise payments, while representatives handle disputed terms and concessions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tariffs, contract exceptions and payment status sat in separate records. Standard features often existed but were poorly connected.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing billing configuration and supported interfaces cover routine cases. AI coding can shorten adapter development, but financial controls still need testing.
tasks.still_hard: Contract-specific pricing, failed payments, duplicate collection prevention and financial reconciliation need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain an unexpected bill and agree a fair response when standard terms do not fit.

ambition.what: Proactive billing-clarity calls before a disputed invoice becomes overdue.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from lookup and calculation toward billing exceptions and customer explanations. No new authority to waive charges or extend credit is assumed.

reach.task: Investigate unmatched payments and disputed balances.
reach.learn: Payment allocation, reconciliation and the boundary between service concessions and credit decisions.

evidence.claim: Tariff calculation, invoice generation and payment-status matching generally use fixed rules.
Automatic charge routing exists in hospitality software; this supports a narrow configuration pattern, not general billing coverage.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where an automated decision has legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: Step shares estimate representative time across the task mix, including occasional exceptions.
The structured-input prior fits billing, but customer explanation remains a material part of today's work.
Customer payment authorisation is not representative time; payment assistance moves to self-service.
Build ranges cover one service family and supported interfaces, not replacement of financial systems.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access review and any consultation required by national rules are included.
unknowns: Available tariff rules and contract exceptions.
Supported payment methods and interface access.
Existing customer authorisation records and payment mandates.
Current concession limits and approval roles.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which existing billing settings cover the current service catalogue?
How do interfaces prevent duplicate invoices or payment attempts?
Which billing decisions require a person because of their effects?
new_work: Maintain tariff and tax mappings.
Investigate failed or unmatched payments.
Check reconciliation totals and duplicate-prevention logs.
Review pricing exceptions and access changes.
tasks.statement: Determine charges for services requested, collect deposits or payments, or arrange for billing.

tasks.short: Prepare contracts, update addresses and issue service discontinuance orders.

steps.what: Read the customer's contract, address-change or cancellation request.
Verify the requester and find the relevant account and contract.
Check required fields, notice periods and supporting documents.
Populate the applicable contract form, address record or discontinuance instruction.
Resolve missing evidence, conflicting details or nonstandard terms.
Save verified address changes and routine account details.
Check and issue the discontinuance order when cancellation applies.
Send the prepared contract for signature when a new agreement applies.
Send confirmation and file the completed change record.

tasks.design: Configure authenticated change forms in the {HELPDESK}, validate fields against the {CRM} and {CLM}, and generate documents from approved {DOCS} templates. Verified address changes update automatically; discontinuance orders require representative approval before reaching the {OPS_SYSTEM}, and contracts take effect after signature through the {ESIGN}. Confirmation and filing follow the completed branch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived without complete fields, and representatives copied the same details between forms and records.
tasks.enabler_now: Authenticated forms, templates and existing workflow settings cover most changes. Small deterministic adapters connect records without needing language generation.
tasks.still_hard: Identity exceptions, joint account authority, nonstandard terms and cancellation consequences need people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a formally complete request still has unclear authority or harmful consequences.

ambition.what: Customers who need to make routine address changes outside staffed hours.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer forms and more authority or contract exceptions. No new right to change contract terms is assumed.

reach.task: Prepare formal service-change confirmations.
reach.learn: Approved wording, document version control and evidence of delivery.

evidence.claim: Customer-service software can change addresses through integrations.
Validated fields and approved templates support deterministic document preparation.
Legal or similarly significant solely automated decisions require an Article 22 assessment.

assumptions: Contract, address and cancellation work are alternative branches; shares estimate time across their combined mix.
Only applicable branch artefacts are required for confirmation.
Structured forms replace routine email intake. Free-text and identity exceptions go to a person.
The low model-need prior fits this task; no model loop is proposed.
Build ranges cover one contract template family and one service-change interface.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access and consultation under applicable national rules are included.
unknowns: Existing authenticated customer channels.
Identity checks and delegated account authority.
Contract templates and notice-period rules.
Which service terminations require specialist approval.
Available interfaces and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which change types can existing software handle through configuration?
How are updates propagated and reversed when one downstream system fails?
Which cancellation consequences require additional human assessment?
new_work: Maintain templates and validation rules.
Handle identity and authority exceptions.
Review discontinuance orders.
Resolve failed updates and unsigned contracts.
Audit a sample of completed changes.
tasks.statement: Complete contract forms, prepare change of address records, or issue service discontinuance orders, using computers.

tasks.short: Gather complaint evidence, examine possible causes and assess whether the complaint is valid.

steps.what: Hear the customer's complaint and clarify the disputed outcome during a call.
Retrieve billing, service events and previous contacts across {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}.
Request missing readings, dates or supporting documents through {EMAIL}.
Compare charges, dates and usage in a worksheet; flag unexplained differences.
Read contextual evidence and service policies to identify plausible causes.

loop.input: Reconciled records, complaint narrative, service policies and relevant context evidence.
loop.output: An evidence-linked list of plausible causes, contradictions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require sources for factual claims; the representative checks alternatives and rejects unsupported causal conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; insufficient or contradictory evidence returns to manual investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative complaints and context vary; fixed checks cannot explain every service event or competing account.

steps.what: Assess complaint validity and decide whether specialist investigation is needed.
Record findings and route unresolved causes to the responsible service team.

tasks.design: Deterministic integrations assemble a dated evidence pack from {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}, then calculate billing and usage differences. A bounded reading loop compares the pack with policies in {DOCS} and drafts possible explanations with sources and uncertainties. The representative assesses validity, while {HELPDESK} records the approved findings and routes unresolved questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was split across teams and records, and contextual explanations required manual reading after basic reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development makes evidence assembly cheaper, while bounded drafting can organise varied narratives without deciding validity.
tasks.still_hard: Missing readings, conflicting accounts and separating correlation from cause remain difficult. Weather alone cannot establish why an individual bill changed.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh conflicting evidence, hear what the customer disputes and recognise when a plausible explanation is insufficient.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of recurring billing causes for service operations investigation.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time testing explanations and resolving disputed facts. They can prioritise investigation referrals within agreed limits; refund and policy-exception authority require separate delegation.

reach.task: Reproduce a suspected billing or account-display defect from a complaint.
reach.learn: Write reproducible steps, preserve event timelines and distinguish a data defect from a policy disagreement.

evidence.claim: Customer-service tools can answer questions and access order information through integrations.
A documented support-assistant study found higher issues resolved per hour; this does not establish accurate complaint-validity decisions.
Deterministic reconciliation plus reviewed explanation drafting is a proposed design; causal validity still needs human assessment.

assumptions: The illustrated company has billing and service-event records; weather evidence is relevant only for some complaints.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates, with substantial retrieval effort but persistent judgement work.
The worksheet ties records together where existing screens lack a cross-record comparison.
The design supports assessment and referral; it does not automatically reject complaints or issue refunds.
No new call recording, emotion recognition or employee performance scoring is introduced.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access and any employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which records share reliable customer, account and event identifiers?
Are tariffs, readings and service events complete and historically versioned?
Which contextual evidence is available and licensed for use?
What assessment, escalation and remedy authority does each role hold?
Which data access and employee consultation processes apply?
research_questions: Which recurring complaint causes can be tested with deterministic checks?
Does the evidence pack reduce investigation time while preserving contradictory evidence?
How often do drafted explanations suggest a cause unsupported by the record?
new_work: Review proposed causes and evidence gaps.
Maintain tariff rules, evidence checklists and routing.
Resolve missing identifiers and failed evidence retrieval.
Sample assessments for unsupported explanations and missed alternatives.
tasks.statement: Obtain and examine all relevant information to assess validity of complaints and to determine possible causes, such as extreme weather conditions that could increase utility bills.

tasks.short: Offer relevant additional products or services during customer interactions.

steps.what: Review the customer's current services and contact preferences in {CRM}.
Decide whether an additional offer fits the customer and current interaction.
Ask about needs and listen during a customer call.
Explain a suitable offer, its price and limitations; address customer questions.
Record needs, interest and agreed follow-up in {CRM}.

loop.input: Brief representative notes and the selected offer.
loop.output: Structured needs, expressed interest and agreed follow-up, with unknown fields left blank.
loop.check: Validate catalogue identifiers; the representative confirms interest and follow-up before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; incomplete notes use a structured form.
loop.why_not_simpler: Brief narrative notes vary; a bounded extraction avoids retyping them into several fields.

steps.what: Create a follow-up lead and assign it to a sales representative in {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure {CRM} to show current services, contact preferences and rule-eligible offers beside the customer record. The representative chooses whether to raise an offer and conducts the conversation; a bounded loop converts their notes into a reviewed interest record. Existing {CRM} routing then assigns the agreed follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service history and offer conditions took time to assemble, while conversational judgement offered little scope for fixed automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration can assemble account context, and small extraction loops can reduce repeated note entry.
tasks.still_hard: Timing, trust, suitability and responding to hesitation remain human work. Catalogue and eligibility data must stay current.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when the customer needs help rather than an offer, and explain trade-offs without pressure.

ambition.what: Customers whose existing service duplicates or exceeds their stated needs.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching and logging, with most conversation time retained. They gain a clearer basis for choosing a helpful offer; pricing and contract authority do not expand.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Coach representatives on offer timing and customer outcomes.
reach.learn: Review conversation examples, distinguish expressed interest from consent, and assess suitability beyond conversion.

evidence.claim: A customer-facing shopping assistant exists, but this does not demonstrate equivalent performance in human service conversations.
A documented support-assistant study found productivity gains, especially for novices; it did not establish sales conversion gains.
Account briefs, eligibility filters and lead routing can use deterministic configuration.

assumptions: This is occasional additional-service solicitation during support work, not a primary sales role.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates; live conversation dominates this task.
The baseline uses representative notes and does not introduce call recording or employee scoring.
Known eligibility, contact preferences and duplicate-service checks can be expressed as rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules govern any consultation required by later recording or monitoring changes.
unknowns: Are service holdings, prices and eligibility rules available together?
Which contact preferences and marketing permissions must be enforced?
Can representatives suggest lower-cost alternatives as well as additional services?
Which access and consultation approvals apply?
research_questions: Does the account brief reduce preparation time without increasing unsuitable offers?
Would a structured form be faster than note extraction for the team's actual notes?
Which customer outcome measures reveal pressure or poor suitability?
new_work: Confirm extracted interest and follow-up details.
Maintain catalogue eligibility, pricing and routing rules.
Resolve duplicate leads and stale account data.
Review examples of unsuitable offers for coaching.
tasks.statement: Solicit sales of new or additional services or products.

tasks.short: Review policy terms and loss evidence to assess insurance coverage.

steps.what: Retrieve the policy version and loss record from the insurance administration system {OTHER}.
Read policy documents and endorsements to identify relevant terms.

loop.input: The applicable policy wording, endorsements and loss record.
loop.output: Relevant clauses with quotations, page references and unresolved terms.
loop.check: Verify quotations against the source and document version; a representative checks clause relevance.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting wording goes to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clause relevance depends on varied wording and endorsements; fixed keyword rules miss material context.

steps.what: Request missing loss details through {EMAIL}.
Compare loss evidence with coverage, exclusions and conditions; write a provisional assessment.

loop.input: Reviewed clauses, loss facts, evidence and approved interpretation guidance.
loop.output: A provisional coverage assessment separating facts, interpretations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every material statement links to evidence or a clause; a representative checks omissions and reasoning.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguity or unsupported conclusions require manual assessment.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applying narrative exclusions to disputed facts requires contextual interpretation beyond fixed coverage rules.

steps.what: Approve the coverage determination within delegated authority or escalate disputed interpretation.
Record and send the approved coverage explanation through {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: An integration retrieves the applicable policy and loss records from {OTHER}; a bounded reading loop produces cited clauses and a provisional assessment in {HELPDESK}. A claims handler approves the determination, after which templates record and send the approved explanation through {HELPDESK} and {EMAIL}. Evidence requests have their own approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy versions, endorsements and loss evidence were scattered, while interpretation could not safely be reduced to lookup rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster integration development and bounded document reading reduce retrieval and drafting effort. Policy interpretation still needs accountable review.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting endorsements, disputed facts and consequential coverage decisions remain expensive to assess.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when literal wording misses the material facts, explain uncertainty and take responsibility for the determination.

ambition.what: A pre-submission evidence check for customers with incomplete loss notifications.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time resolving missing evidence and explaining difficult cases. They can prioritise evidence collection; binding coverage rights remain with the delegated claims role.

reach.task: Prepare clear coverage notices from approved determinations.
reach.learn: Cited drafting, accessible explanations and the distinction between an assessment and an approved decision.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based question answering with handover is available; this does not establish reliable insurance coverage interpretation.
Retrieval, cited drafting and human coverage approval are a proposed design, without an insurance-specific case in the digest.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its exceptions.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to an insurance service team, rather than every customer service department.
Today's steps and time shares are estimates for a mid-size European company.
Representatives assess routine cases; a delegated claims role approves consequential determinations.
The high automation prior overstates substitution here because policy interpretation and approval retain substantial human time.
Build ranges cover one policy family and one connected insurance administration system.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Which policy versions and endorsements are accessible in machine-readable form?
Which coverage decisions can representatives legally and operationally approve?
Are medical or other special-category data present?
Which access approvals and employee consultation processes apply?
research_questions: How often do reviewed clause suggestions omit a material exclusion or endorsement?
Which evidence checks can be expressed as reliable fixed rules?
Does assisted assessment improve explanation quality without increasing incorrect coverage conclusions?
new_work: Review clause selection and provisional assessments.
Maintain policy versions, evidence checklists and approved interpretations.
Investigate conflicting documents and unsupported citations.
Check access controls, retention and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Review insurance policy terms to determine whether a particular loss is covered by insurance.

tasks.short: Match disputed goods to order records and prepare the appropriate return credit document.

steps.what: Read the merchandise dispute and attachments in {HELPDESK}.

loop.output: Claimed order references, disputed items, quantities and reasons, each linked to its source.
loop.check: Match references to account records; a representative confirms ambiguous items and quantities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved identifiers go to manual intake.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers describe goods and disputes in varied prose and attachment layouts.

steps.what: Retrieve the customer order, original invoice and shipment record from {ERP}.
Inspect disputed goods against the shipment record and record their condition.
Reconcile disputed items, quantities and prices in a return worksheet.
Approve the return value and any policy exception.
Prepare and post the credit note linked to the original invoice in {ERP}.
Send the credit note and update the customer case through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A bounded intake loop in {HELPDESK} identifies disputed lines, while deterministic integration matches them to orders and invoices in {ERP} and inspections in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Fixed checks calculate the proposed credit and detect duplicate or excessive returns; people inspect goods and approve return exceptions and value. After approval, {ERP} generates the credit note and {HELPDESK} sends the matching notice.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer descriptions, warehouse findings and financial records lacked shared identifiers, so staff reconciled them manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing return functions can handle posting and document generation; inexpensive integration and bounded extraction connect the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, disputed quantities, partial returns and responsibility for damage still require evidence and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve contested condition or responsibility fairly, and recognise when the standard return policy produces an unreasonable outcome.

ambition.what: A customer-visible return status covering inspection, authorisation and credit issuance.

tasks.altitude: The representative handles disputed evidence and customer explanations instead of copying financial lines. They can resolve reconciliation exceptions within existing limits; credit approval rights stay delegated.

reach.task: Reconcile return credits against outstanding customer balances.
reach.learn: Credit-note allocation, duplicate-credit controls and the difference between a credit and a cash refund.

evidence.claim: Document-based order capture can validate customer, stock and price data and route exceptions before posting.
Order import and stock synchronisation already exist, supporting deterministic record exchange.
Return reconciliation and approved credit-note generation are proposed extensions; the digest provides no direct returns case.

assumptions: This task applies to a company handling physical goods.
A credit note is the usual return document here; the required document depends on the transaction and national rules.
The worksheet represents manual reconciliation between departments, not a replacement for financial records in {ERP}.
Time shares describe the full handoff chain, including warehouse and finance work.
Build ranges cover one order flow, one warehouse connection and established return rules.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national employee consultation requirements must be checked where working practices change.
unknowns: Does {ERP} support linked partial credits and prevent cumulative over-crediting?
Who approves routine returns and which exceptions need supervisor approval?
Are inspection results linked to individual order lines?
Which tax treatments, document formats and access approvals apply?
research_questions: What share of disputes can match directly to an original invoice line?
Which exceptions arise from missing identifiers rather than genuine judgement?
Can existing {ERP} return configuration remove the need for custom posting code?
new_work: Review uncertain item extraction and unmatched lines.
Maintain return rules and approval limits.
Investigate duplicate credits, failed postings and reconciliation differences.
Keep warehouse inspection identifiers aligned with financial order lines.
tasks.statement: Compare disputed merchandise with original requisitions and information from invoices and prepare invoices for returned goods.

tasks.short: Recommend practical changes that prevent recurring product, packaging, shipping, service or billing problems.

steps.what: Review recurring complaints and select examples showing a preventable problem.

loop.input: A fixed batch of complaint records and case notes, with unnecessary personal details removed.
loop.output: Suggested problem groups, counts and linked problem examples.
loop.check: Verify record links and counts mechanically; representative checks themes against source cases.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction per batch; unresolved cases remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing categories support counting, but inconsistent free text needs interpretation to reveal specific recurring problems.

steps.what: Check affected orders and shipments for packaging, delivery and handling patterns.
Check invoices, credits and corrections to establish billing patterns and recorded costs.
Discuss likely causes and practical constraints with relevant operations, finance or product colleagues.
Compare possible changes and select a recommendation using impact, effort and customer consequences.
Write a recommendation with supporting examples, expected effects and a proposed trial.

loop.input: Selected recommendation, linked evidence, feasibility notes and a fixed proposal template.
loop.output: Draft improvement proposal with a trial question and proposed success measure.
loop.check: Populate figures deterministically; require source links and representative review of claims and assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence remains marked for completion by the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles structure, but explaining varied causes and tradeoffs requires short, case-specific prose.

steps.what: Review the proposal and agree whether to sponsor a trial with the process owner.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins authorised {HELPDESK} cases to {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} records, calculates counts and recorded costs, and presents linked evidence in {BI}. A bounded classification loop suggests complaint themes for review, and an artefact generator drafts the chosen proposal in {DOCS}. The representative selects the recommendation; the service supervisor and relevant process owner decide whether to sponsor a trial.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaint text, shipment details and billing corrections sit in separate records. Joining them and preparing a credible proposal often takes more effort than the recommendation itself.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports or APIs support deterministic joins and calculations. Bounded models can group complaint text and draft explanations, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building these connections.
tasks.still_hard: A recurring complaint does not prove its cause. Incomplete identifiers, unrecorded costs and competing operational priorities still require investigation and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The representative understands what customers experienced and can challenge a convenient explanation. Colleagues establish operational feasibility and accept responsibility for changes.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which recurring billing or shipping problem merits a small prevention trial.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing explanations with colleagues. No formal decision rights change: spending and process changes still require the relevant owners.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Define a small service-improvement trial and review its results.
reach.learn: Baseline selection, trial measures, workload effects and how to distinguish improvement from changes in case mix.

reach.task: Revise standard replies after a recurring service problem is understood.
reach.learn: Template control, clear customer explanations and when a reply needs individual handling.

evidence.claim: Joining records, calculating counts and generating proposal templates are deterministic implementation patterns; these build estimates are indicative.
Integration-backed customer support can retrieve order information today; this supports lookup feasibility, not automatic root-cause discovery.
A documented support study found higher issue-resolution productivity with an assistant; it does not establish equivalent gains for improvement recommendations.
Dutch works-council consent requirements can apply to agent dashboards and call recording; other countries require assessment under national rules.

assumptions: The workflow represents a mid-size European company with separate support, operations and finance records.
Time shares are illustrative shares of this task, including supervisory review, rather than measured shares of the representative's week.
The analysis supplements recorded complaint categories with free-text grouping; it does not require an autonomous agent.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot with existing infrastructure, not replacement of core systems.
GDPR applies to personal data throughout. Access is limited, unnecessary personal details are removed, and retention is defined.
Consultation follows national rules where applicable. The design analyses service problems rather than scoring employee performance.
unknowns: Which systems permit exports or APIs and who can authorise access.
Whether complaint records contain reliable order and invoice identifiers.
Whether packaging defects, shipping failures and correction costs are recorded consistently.
Who approves trials, spending and changes across service, operations, product and finance.
Which national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements apply.
Available complaint volumes, languages and existing reporting capabilities.
research_questions: Can existing categories and reports identify useful recurring problems before adding text classification?
How accurately do proposed themes reflect a representative sample of source complaints?
Which recommendations produce measurable reductions in repeat complaints after accounting for order volume and case mix?
new_work: Review suggested themes and investigate unmatched records.
Maintain category definitions, join rules and integration access.
Check proposal claims, source links and unsupported causal explanations.
Refresh reference samples when products, policies or complaint language change.
Track trial results with process owners and retire changes that do not help.
tasks.statement: Recommend improvements in products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing methods and procedures to prevent future problems.

tasks.short: Answer customer questions, take orders, process cancellations and gather complaint details.

steps.what: Greet the customer and verify identity where account access requires it.
Find account, order and product information across service screens.
Explain options and establish what the customer wants.
For orders, check items and prices, then submit the confirmed order.
For cancellations, check terms and customer confirmation, then close the account.
For complaints, ask what happened and what remedy the customer seeks.
Assign the complaint to the responsible queue and record the promised response date.

tasks.design: Show a joined customer view in the {HELPDESK}, using controlled reads from the {CRM}, {ERP} and approved material in the {DOCS}. Configure order forms and complaint routing, and connect cancellation actions through the {WORKFLOW}; the representative approves orders and cancellations before they take effect. Keep live conversations human, with information and paperwork ready on screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account information, policies and transaction screens were separate. Connecting them required costly mapping and agreement about who could change an account.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and routing can handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector development effort where stable interfaces exist.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, conflicting account terms and incomplete data still cause exceptions. Upset customers and disputed cancellation consequences need a person.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, establish the customer's real request and explain consequences without pressuring them.

ambition.what: Cancellation consequence preview during the customer conversation

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer screen searches and repeated entries, with more time to clarify requests. The representative gains no new approval rights by default; they can explain cancellation consequences before committing the change.

reach.task: Resolve routine visitor questions before transferring them.
reach.learn: Learn the service directory, identity boundaries and transfer criteria.

reach.task: Check booking changes and explain their consequences.
reach.learn: Learn availability rules, fare conditions and customer confirmation requirements.

evidence.claim: Connected support systems can retrieve order information and perform account-related actions.
Order imports and stock synchronisation are established capabilities.
An assistant study found higher support productivity, with larger gains for novices; it does not predict this design's savings.
The proposed deterministic design and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The steps cover alternative inquiry, order, cancellation and complaint paths; time shares average across that mix.
Telephone is the representative channel shown; an in-person desk follows comparable boundaries.
Structured transaction forms suffice, so this design needs no model loop.
The conversation-heavy prior remains useful, but information retrieval and transaction entry can change independently.
GDPR applies to customer data. Access is limited to the case and the representative's role.
Build ranges are working-day effort for a limited pilot. National employee consultation applies where required; new recording or monitoring is outside this design.
unknowns: Which customer and transaction systems are authoritative?
Are supported read and write interfaces available?
Which orders and cancellations may representatives approve?
What identity checks and cancellation terms apply?
What is the actual channel and request mix?
What access approvals and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing forms and routing remove custom development?
Which cancellation consequences can be calculated from authoritative account terms?
Can integrations retry safely without duplicating orders or cancellations?
new_work: Review prepared orders and cancellations before committing them.
Resolve mismatched customer records and failed integrations.
Maintain routing rules, account-term mappings and approved information.
tasks.statement: Confer with customers by telephone or in person to provide information about products or services, take or enter orders, cancel accounts, or obtain details of complaints.

role_batches.altitude: The representative spends less time finding facts, copying records and chasing updates, and more time clarifying requests and judging whether remedies worked. Existing transaction and adjustment limits remain; broader corrective-action rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Prepare evidence-based correspondence with correspondence clerks.
Verify customer outcomes with computer user support specialists.
Recommend process corrections to first-line supervisors.
Coordinate accessible callbacks with switchboard operators.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish customer statements from verified facts.
Review drafts for accuracy, privacy and unintended promises.
Capture remedies as observable outcomes.
Handle integration exceptions and duplicate-action risks.
Explain adverse outcomes and check understanding.
Analyse recurring failures and recommend corrective action.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Become a resolution specialist who uses joined case evidence to identify failed remedies, organise accessible explanation callbacks and propose process corrections. Broader remedy authority is granted explicitly by the service supervisor.

role_batches.altitude: The role spends less time moving records and more time explaining bills, resolving difficult complaints and securing investigation ownership. Financial and contractual decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Credit clerks: reconcile payment problems without drifting into unsupported credit decisions.
Correspondence clerks: produce clear formal responses backed by case evidence.
First-line supervisors: identify recurring complaint causes and assess exceptional remedies.
Computer user support specialists: provide evidence that makes technical escalations investigable.
skills_to_grow: Read joined customer and transaction records.
Check financial actions and recognise duplicate or failed transactions.
Apply consumer rights and delegated approval limits.
Review source-linked summaries and drafted explanations.
Handle difficult conversations and negotiate investigation ownership.
Measure repeat complaints and remedy outcomes.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A customer recovery specialist who combines accurate billing, effective remedies and clear escalation evidence, then proposes specific process fixes from recurring complaints.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult conversations, evidence disputes and explanation quality. Better preparation supports broader investigation work, while financial and coverage decision rights remain explicitly delegated.
reach: Prepare clear, approved correspondence with a correspondence clerk.
Reconcile return credits with a credit clerk.
Turn recurring complaints into reproducible investigations with a computer user support specialist.
Support customer-outcome coaching with a first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers.
skills_to_grow: Read source-linked evidence and challenge unsupported conclusions.
Understand billing, return and coverage rules within delegated authority.
Conduct needs-led conversations and explain uncertainty clearly.
Write reproducible referrals and recognise recurring service failures.
Review structured records and identify integration exceptions.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A service resolution specialist who combines customer conversations with evidence analysis, runs a recurring complaint-cause review and proposes targeted service improvements.

role_batches.altitude: Customer service representatives contribute stronger evidence to prevention discussions and spend more time investigating causes. Operational approval rights remain with supervisors and process owners.
reach: Help service supervisors define and evaluate small prevention trials.
Help correspondence clerks update standard replies from confirmed service findings.
skills_to_grow: Root-cause questioning
Basic trial design and measurement
Reading operational and billing evidence
Writing concise recommendations
Cross-team negotiation
role_batches.ambitious_version: A representative becomes a regular contributor to a weekly prevention review, bringing one evidenced problem and a measurable trial proposal.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
